label: Monitor
name: monitor
description: A monitor of observed HTTP calls: the routes talk to a REST API (mockapi.io); entries are imported from and exported to CSV files through the blob registry. Reads are public; writes are for signed-in employees holding the recorder role, identified by our own token, issued by the included access tree (@wilanis/access) at /api/v1/auth-employees against a directory this project binds (customers sign in at /api/v1/auth-customers and hold a token too, but no write). Preferences live in the session. A command-line greeting is gated by a one-time code. Plugins come from npm packages named by "from".

otp.description: a one-time code: printed by the issue-otp command in this example, delivered out of band in a real tree -- the binding of access.port.json#deliverCode decides

includes.description: sign-in, sessions, policies and the one-time code, as a tree of their own; identity.port.json is bound below, in features/directories

startup.label: Prepare the entry store
startup.description: Make storage ready once, before anything reads it: under local that creates the collections the store declares, and under live there is nothing to create, so it reads the collection once. Only a startup step prepares, and only because project.json says so.

startup.label: Reach the entry store
startup.description: Read the entries once before the HTTP server opens, so a tree whose storage is unreachable refuses to serve instead of answering every route with a fault. The port is bound per profile, so this checks whatever storage the profile chose.

startup.label: Watch for changes
startup.description: Serve the tree again whenever a document changes, without closing the port. A change that does not pass wilanis check is reported and the last good tree keeps answering.

startup.label: Listen
startup.description: Open the HTTP port and answer this tree's routes. Delete this step and nothing listens: a tree serves because it says so, never because a trigger exists.

live.description: The real monitor API, and the directories written in the connections. A production profile binds identity.port.json to a binding whose connections are an OIDC issuer and LDAP; nothing else changes.

local.description: Everything in this process: the entries kept in memory, and the directories written in the connections. Nothing reaches the network, so `wilanis start example --profile local` serves the same routes with no upstream at all.
